note: Snapshot of the live Aperture MCP server (initialize + tools/list). Regenerate with landing/scripts/snapshot-tools.sh.

server.name: aperture
server.title: Aperture
server.description: A safe way for AI agents to work in web systems that have no API. Every change is previewed, checked, read back, and undoable.

instructions: Aperture is for changing records in a web admin portal or legacy business system that has no API: resident lists, user lists, customer or inventory screens, registrar pages. What it does that driving the page by hand does not: it turns the page into typed tools, shows what a change will affect before it happens (including records that go with it), reads the system back afterwards and compares it with the prediction, gives a receipt, and can undo. Reading is open: compile_site works on any public page without setup. Signing in and changing anything only happen on systems the operator listed, through the owner's authority. Start with find_systems (what you need, in plain words) or compile_site (a page address), then find to get exact keys, then delete or create with dry_run first. Compile every page whose records a change touches. Not for: systems that have a real API, sites you are not allowed to automate, or CAPTCHA and sign-in steps (a person does those).

tools.name: get_instructions
tools.description: Start here. Returns a short guide to this system, the record kinds, and the rules. Read it once.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Look up records. Returns small typed items with their unique keys. Names are not unique: always act on the key. Free, nothing changes.

kind.description: Record kind, as compile_site or find_systems named it (for example residents or devices). Call compile_site first if you have none.

query.description: Text to match in any field, like a name. Leave empty to list.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Delete one record by key. With dry_run: true it only previews: what is removed, the count change, which rule applies. Nothing changes. To commit, call again with the plan_id. For most jobs use apply, which does both when the rules allow.

kind.description: Record kind, as compile_site or find_systems named it (for example residents or devices). Call compile_site first if you have none.

key.description: The unique key from find, like S014. Never a name.

plan_id.description: Commit a plan you already previewed.

tools.name: create
tools.description: Create one record. The record needs a unique key. With dry_run: true it only previews. To commit, call again with the plan_id.

kind.description: Record kind, as compile_site or find_systems named it (for example residents or devices). Call compile_site first if you have none.

record.description: Fields of the new record. Must include a unique key.

tools.name: publish
tools.description: Send staged changes to the outside world (for example to devices, a gate, or another system). It always needs the owner. Without plan_id it previews and asks the owner. It cannot be undone.

tools.name: compile_site
tools.description: Point Aperture at a web page and it reads the page's forms, read-only, and turns each one into a typed record you can fill. Only works on hosts the operator has authorized. It never submits anything and never tries to get past a CAPTCHA: a person does that. Returns each form's id, fields (label, type, required, allowed values) and submit button.

url.description: The page address. With login set, this is the sign-in page. Leave it out to read the current page again (after a submit, or when a page changed).

login.description: Name of a login the operator stored on the server. You never see the password.

then.description: With login: the page to compile after signing in.

tools.name: apply
tools.description: The normal way to make a change. Previews inside the server. If the rules allow it, it commits at once and returns a receipt with a read-back. If a person must decide, it returns awaiting_approval with a plan_id to poll with get_plan.

patch.description: For update: the fields to change, like { city: 'Leeds' }.

tools.name: apply_batch
tools.description: Apply many changes in one call. Everything inside the rules commits. Items that need the owner are listed with plan_ids. Refusals are listed with next moves. Stops at the first failed commit. Returns one summary, so you do not need many round trips.

patch.description: For update: the fields to change, like { city: 'Leeds' }.

plan_ids.description: Instead of ops: commit plans the owner already approved, in order, with the first `canary` checked first.

dry_run.description: Change nothing. Returns the total blast radius: everything that would be removed, dependents included.

canary.description: Commit only the first N, check they did exactly what was predicted, and halt the rest if any surprised or failed.

tools.name: find_systems
tools.description: Start here when you are not given an address. Describe what you need to do in plain words (for example 'remove a resident from the access list' or 'update a customer record'). Returns the systems you are allowed to work in that match, with the address to compile and any profile other agents shared. It never searches the open web.

need.description: What you need to do or find, in plain words.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Check a plan: awaiting_approval, approved, expired, committed. Use it to wait for the owner's decision instead of retrying. If the outcome of a change is unknown (the server stopped while it ran), this reads the system and says what really happened; it never runs the change again.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this long for the owner to decide, so you do not burn turns polling.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Reverse a committed change using the copy saved before it. Reads the system back to verify. Works within the undo window. Published changes cannot be recalled.

receipt_id.description: The receipt id from the commit result.

tools.name: escalate
tools.description: Ask the owner for help when a rule blocks you, like the daily limit. One message goes out. Keep working on other items. Do not retry the blocked one.

reason.description: One sentence on what you need and why.
